[[Category:Probability distribution]]
[[File:Normal-distribution-p-df.svg|thumbnail|The '''probability density function''' of the normal distribution with different '''parameters''']]
The '''normal distribution''', denoted by $\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma)$ is a [[probability distribution]] over $\mathbb{R}$ with the probability density function

$$
\forall x \in \mathbb{R}: f_X(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}
\exp\left(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),
$$

where $\mu, \sigma \in \mathbb{R}$ are the two parameters of the distribution, corresponding to the '''mean''' and the '''standard deviation''' of the distribution respectively.

$\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ is known as the '''standard normal distribution'''

== Properties ==

=== Symmetry over $x=\mu$ ===

$$
\forall x \in \mathbb{R}: f_X(x)=f_X(2\mu-x)
$$
